title: The one who appeared is God, and the whole Church deserves equal care
english: The one who appeared on earth and lived among human beings was not only human but also God, as Jeremiah the prophet says: “This is our God; no other will be reckoned beside him. He found out the whole way of knowledge and gave it to Jacob his child and to Israel, whom he loved. After this he was seen on earth and lived among human beings” (Jeremiah). When did he live among human beings, if not when he was born together with them from a virgin, shared infancy, grew up together, ate together, drank together, and shared the rest of human life?

For if prayers must be made, he says, for the catholic Church which is from the ends of the world, then all the more must providence be shown for the whole of it, and care and concern must be given equally to all its parts.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius opens by arguing from Jeremiah that the one who appeared on earth and lived among humans is not only human but also God, then turns to the duty of providential care for the whole catholic Church.
